newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: U.S. Navy plans dangerous Antarctic rescue mission.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Navy plans dangerous Antarctic rescue mission.

text.p: The U.S. Navy is planning a dangerous winter flight to Antarctica this week to rescue a U.S. civilian worker who has developed heart problems.

The U.S. Naval Antarctic Support Unit (NASU) in New Zealand said it would attempt its third ever winter landing at the U.S. McMurdo Base, on the Ross Ice Shelf, on Friday or Saturday to evacuate the sick man.
"Any landing in Antarctica is dangerous, but landing during the winter makes it extra dangerous," NASU spokesman Dave Lippman told Reuters.
"This is only the third time we've ever done a flight like this in our history. This is a hazardous undertaking."
The worker, who has not been named, is to be evacuated to Christchurch, New Zealand, for evaluation and treatment.

With the southern winter setting in, Lippman said temperatures at McMurdo Base last week dropped to minus 34 degrees Fahrenheit (-37 Celsius), with a windchill factor as low as minus 97 degrees Fahrenheit (-72 Celsius).
"Those are major-league hazards right there," he said. "Old man weather calls the shots in Antarctica -- that's a fact of life."
Lippman said the last sunset before winter occurred at McMurdo last week and the base would experience short and diminishing periods of twilight until the winter solstice in late June.

McMurdo Station's over-winter party of about 156 people is normally completely isolated until missions resume in August, bringing in personnel and supplies to prepare the Antarctic bases for the summer season.
McMurdo has a population of about 1,000 in summer.
Lippman said the rescue flight was still being planned and the type of aircraft to be used had not yet been chosen.

The landing will take place at the Pegasus Runway on the Ross Ice Shelf near McMurdo Station. The runway, usually used only during the Antarctic summer season from October to February, was being readied for the mission, he said.
NASU, based in Christchurch on New Zealand's South Island, is part of U.S. Naval Support Force Antarctica, which provides logistic support to the U.S. Antarctic Programme.
